text: College Cloud Champ Details - Champ (Student) -1 Details Champ Name: A T Abbilaash Age: 20 Gender: Male Department: Department of Computer Science and Engineering Year of Study: 3 Email: abbilaashat@gmail.com Email (Official): 23n201@psgtech.ac.in Mobile Number: 8667093591 Why do you want to be a College Cloud Champ? I want to become a College Cloud Champ because I have always been curious about how technology works and how it can be used to create real-world solutions. My journey began with developing web applications, where I focused on building practical projects that solved small but important problems. While working on these projects, I integrated AWS services like EC2 and S3 to host applications, store data securely, and make them scalable. This hands-on experience showed me the true power of the cloud and motivated me to explore AWS more deeply. One of the projects I am particularly proud of is a Library Feedback System that I developed along with my teammates for our college. We used AWS services to host and scale the application so students and faculty could easily share feedback in a secure and reliable way. This project gave me a deeper understanding on how the cloud can transform even simple campus systems into impactful solutions. Currently, I am also working on building a blockchain solution in Ethereum, where I am leveraging AWS to manage deployment and scalability. Exploring how blockchain and cloud can come together has been an exciting challenge and has opened my eyes to how AWS supports not only web applications but also emerging technologies. One thing I admire about Amazon is the “Day One” principle. It reflects staying curious, open to learning, and willing to innovate as if it were the very first day. I personally connect with this mindset because I never stop experimenting and asking questions. For example, when I first explored serverless computing, I deployed a basic function with AWS Lambda just to understand how it works. This curiosity-driven approach helps me learn quickly and share my learnings with others. Leadership is another quality I strongly believe in. In my project groups, I naturally take the lead in coordinating tasks, breaking down problems, and motivating teammates. Beyond projects, I have also organized hackathons and technical events in my college clubs, where I encouraged students to experiment, build, and showcase their creativity. These experiences taught me how to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels comfortable contributing ideas and learning from each other. As a Cloud Champ, I would like to extend this leadership to the larger student community by organizing workshops, hackathons, and study circles around AWS. My goal is to make cloud computing less intimidating and more approachable for my peers. For me, being a Cloud Champ is not just about improving my own skills—it is about creating a culture of learning and innovation in my college.
